newsitem.title: USA: Former Ill. tollway agency head found guilty.
newsitem.headline: Former Ill. tollway agency head found guilty.

text.p: A DuPage County judge Wednesday convicted former Illinois Tollway Executive Director Robert Hickman and current state Rep. Joseph Kotlarz of taking $190,000 of tollway funds through a public land sale.

Hickman faced eight counts of theft or official misconduct in the bench trial before Judge Ronald Mehling, who convicted the former executive director on four of the counts, a secretary to the judge said Thursday.
Mehling is to consider the remaining counts against Hickman at sentencing.

Kotlarz, D-Chicago, must resign from the House at sentencing under Illinois law. He was convicted on one of five counts against him, the secretary said. The remaining counts will be considered at sentencing, she added.
Both could face anything from probation to 15 years in prison on the convictions. Sentencing has been scheduled for June 12 before Mehling.
According to prosecutors, Kotlarz represented a private company that sought to buy land the tollway authority did not need.

While willing to pay more than $4 million for the land, the company paid $3.8 million for the land and a $240,000 brokerage fee, only part of which went to the real estate company that handled the deal.
